A process reports success through its **exit code** — `0` for success, non-zero
for a problem — and its messages through two streams: **stdout** for normal
output, **stderr** for errors. The inventory CLI exits `1` when a stock check
fails and writes the offending product to stderr. Run it yourself and check the
exit code with `$?`:

```terminal
$ uv run python tools/inventory.py check --min-stock 10
low stock: desk-lamp has 8 (< 10)
$ echo $?
1
```

The error text went to stderr; the exit code says the check failed. Your test
asserts on both.

## Task 1 — Assert failing exit codes and stderr

**Goal:** create `checks/exitcodes.robot` with two tests: one running a stock
check that fails (exit `1`, offending product on stderr), and one running the
CLI's `fail` command (exit `1`).

Here is the same shape — one passing run, one failing run. Adapt it.

<!-- example -->
```robotframework
*** Settings ***
Library    Process

*** Test Cases ***
Good Run Exits Zero
    ${ok}=    Run Process    python3    tools/inventory.py    list
    Should Be Equal As Integers    ${ok.rc}    0

Bad Run Exits One
    ${bad}=    Run Process    python3    tools/inventory.py    fail
    Should Be Equal As Integers    ${bad.rc}    1
    Should Not Be Empty    ${bad.stderr}
```
<!-- /example -->

**Check:** both failing-process tests are defined.

<!-- hint -->
Run the stock check with its flags as separate cells:
`Run Process    python3    tools/inventory.py    check    --min-stock    10`.
It exits `1`.
<!-- /hint -->
<!-- hint -->
The low-stock product is written to stderr — assert
`Should Contain    ${result.stderr}    desk-lamp`. Add a second test that runs
`fail` and checks `${result.rc}` is `1`.
<!-- /hint -->
<!-- solution -->
```robotframework
*** Settings ***
Library    Process

*** Test Cases ***
Stock Check Fails With Exit Code One
    ${result}=    Run Process    python3    tools/inventory.py    check    --min-stock    10
    Should Be Equal As Integers    ${result.rc}    1
    Should Contain    ${result.stderr}    desk-lamp

Deliberate Failure Exits One
    ${result}=    Run Process    python3    tools/inventory.py    fail
    Should Be Equal As Integers    ${result.rc}    1
```
<!-- /solution -->

## Task 2 — Run it green

Run:

```bash
uv run robot checks
```

**Check:** the failing checks exit `1`, and the low-stock product appears on stderr.
